newsitem.title: GERMANY: German food oilseeds area may exceed limit-ZMP.
newsitem.headline: German food oilseeds area may exceed limit-ZMP.

text.p: Germany's 1997 area planted to oilseeds for food use may exceed its allocation under the U.S./EU Blair House accord by nearly nine percent, farm price and marketing office ZMP said.
ZMP said the latest combined total of 1,021,689 ha applying to both food and non-food crops was derived from state statistics offices and regional chambers of agriculture.

ZMP arrived at 909,105 ha for food use by deducting 112,584 ha of non-food acreage which it said was the final registration figure published by state intervention board BLE, which is the relevant authority farmers must notify.
Germany may plant a total 836,099 ha of oilseeds for food use under Blair House, otherwise farmers face penalties in the form of cuts in area aid.
The winter rapeseed area for harvesting in 1997 was pegged at 927,934 hectares, up 150,744 ha from plantings a year earlier while the spring rape area dropped to 55,288 ha from 76,435 ha in 1996.
The sunflower area in 1997 was put at 38,467 ha, down from 43,758 last year.
ZMP said its projections differed from a private survey issued by oilseeds farmer lobby UFOP in February, which put food plantings at 740,640 ha, well below the limit.
The conflict remained unresolved for the time being.
The figures reflected most recent plantings data after the effect of winter damage had been factored in.

According to the national statistics office in Wiesbaden, spring re-sowings on areas originally sown to winter rapeseed represented 2.3 percent of the initial area. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
